reader.requirement: At --std 85 the colon is a separator (it needs no space on either side) and must be written where a general format shows it, which in COBOL-85 (with Amendment 1) is the reference modifier of an identifier or function-identifier, ( leftmost-character-position : [length] ); a reference modifier without its colon, and a colon where no format shows one, are refused.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the 2002 invocation operator '::' (inline-method-invocation-2002, COBOL0900) below COBOL-2002

reader.edition-search: The COLON token and refModSpec are shared by every edition (no predicate); grepped COLONCOLON and invocation operator in VersionConformancePass (the one edition gate found); SeparatorRule's '::' spacing check (COBOL2993) has no edition read.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: '::' is the 2002 invocation operator and is refused at 85; the single colon of the reference modifier is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c17_colon_separator covers the conforming colon forms; the missing-colon and misplaced-colon refusals and a function-identifier's reference modifier are not exercised there

reader.notes: Every 1985 colon form probed is accepted and every misplaced or missing colon refused. At --std 85 the unspaced 'N-A::1' is refused with a message about the 2002 invocation operator's spacing rather than the COBOL0900 edition gate the spaced form gets; it is still refused, so this is message wording only.

refuter.evidence: The only 1985 format that shows a colon is the reference modifier; '::' (2002) refused per the reader's c5_ref7. Probes at --std 85: k1 ref-mod on a function-identifier with arguments FUNCTION REVERSE (W-S) (1:2) -> FE; a ref-mod nested in a function argument inside the leftmost position W-S (FUNCTION LENGTH (W-S (1:2)) : 1) -> B; expressions both sides W-S (N-A - 1:N-A + 1) -> ABC; qualified subscripted element then ref-mod W-F OF W-R (N-A + 1) (2:) -> F; W-S(N-A:) -> BCDEF; receiving ref-mod MOVE "Z" TO W-S (6:1) -> ABCDEZ. Refusals: k2 W-S (2 3:1) -> COBOL0001 near ':'; k3 DISPLAY W-S : 2 -> COBOL2269 unexpected ':'. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR7.
